items.q: Match the endocrine condition to the group on this page — 1) Cushing’s 2) Acromegaly 3) Pheochromocytoma 4) Somatostatinoma … A) Endocrinopathy B) Endocrinopathy C) Endocrinopathy D) Endocrinopathy
items.exp: All four named conditions appear in the Endocrinopathies list associated with DM. (Book p926)

items.q: Which of the following is listed under endocrinopathies associated with DM?
items.exp: Hyperparathyroidism is one of the endocrinopathies listed on the page. (Book p926)

items.q: The endocrine list includes Cushing’s, acromegaly, hyperthyroidism, hyperparathyroidism, pheochromocytoma, glucagonoma and ___.
items.exp: Somatostatinoma is the final endocrine condition in the printed list. (Book p926)

items.q: Assess the endocrine list: I Glucagonoma is included. II Somatostatinoma is included.
items.exp: Both glucagonoma and somatostatinoma are listed under endocrinopathies associated with DM. (Book p926)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the genetic diseases listed on the page?
items.exp: Marfan syndrome is not in the printed genetic-disease list; Down’s, Klinefelter’s and Friedreich’s ataxia are. (Book p926)

items.q: Match the genetic disease to its exact place in the printed list — 1) Down’s syndrome 2) Huntington’s 3) Wolfram syndrome 4) Laurence–Moon–Biedl syndrome … A) Listed genetic disease B) Listed genetic disease C) Listed genetic disease D) Listed genetic disease
items.exp: Down’s syndrome, Huntington’s, Wolfram syndrome and Laurence–Moon–Biedl syndrome all appear in the genetic-disease list. (Book p926)

items.q: A question asks for a genetic disease associated with DM from the page rather than an endocrinopathy. Which choice belongs to that genetic list?
items.exp: Myotonic dystrophy appears under genetic disease; the other three choices are in the endocrinopathy list. (Book p926)

items.q: Which condition is printed between Prader Willi and myotonic dystrophy in the genetic list?
items.exp: The genetic list runs Down’s, Klinefelter, Friedreich’s ataxia, Huntington’s, Prader Willi, porphyria, myotonic dystrophy, Wolfram and Laurence–Moon–Biedl. (Book p926)

items.q: How many genetic diseases are visibly listed under the genetic-disease heading?
items.exp: The page lists nine genetic diseases: Down’s, Klinefelter, Friedreich’s ataxia, Huntington’s, Prader Willi, porphyria, myotonic dystrophy, Wolfram syndrome and Laurence–Moon–Biedl syndrome. (Book p926)

items.q: Assess the genetic-disease section: I Porphyria is listed. II Wolfram syndrome is listed.
items.exp: Both porphyria and Wolfram syndrome appear in the genetic-disease list. (Book p926)

items.q: When sorting the page's associations with DM, which label should be placed under the genetic-disease heading?
items.exp: Prader Willi is in the genetic-disease list, while glucagonoma, hyperthyroidism and Cushing’s are in the endocrinopathy list. (Book p926)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the named genetic diseases on this page?
items.exp: Somatostatinoma belongs to the endocrinopathy list; porphyria, Wolfram syndrome and Huntington’s belong to the genetic list. (Book p926)
